1942.desc: Omaha Beach, 6 June 1944, a low morning sun over the sea, broken cloud: a wide grey-sand foreshore (the surf along y 60 to 0, x -800..800) runs south to a low pebble shingle lip (y -1210..-1230), then the concrete seawall (y -1230..-1246, chest-high) with two long ramps at x -400 and x 340 climbing to the promenade. Behind the wall the grassy bluff rises (y -1264..-1580) to a flat crest with a concrete bunker at x -150, y -1800 looking down the beach. Steel hedgehogs and anti-boat posts dot the surf and wet sand; barbed wire lies across the shingle; a Sherman and a jeep burn where they died. Smoke haze, grey light, no cover. The exits are the breaches; everything between the water and the wire is open ground.
